Nate: heads up — found a weird mypy/pyright discrepancy with the autogenerated python models in async clients. when a response field is typed as Optional[Union[str, List[str]]], pyright narrows it differently inside async iterator handlers and mypy blows up in sampleapp tests
Maria: details? small repro? :thinking_face:
Nate: yeah, minimal repro below. run mypy vs pyright

```py
# repro.py
from typing import Optional, Union, AsyncIterator

class AutoModel:
    tags: Optional[Union[str, list[str]]]

async def stream(models: AsyncIterator[AutoModel]):
    async for m in models:
        # mypy: error: "list[str]" not compatible with "str" (when checking branches)
        if isinstance(m.tags, list):
            print(m.tags[0])
        else:
            print(m.tags.upper())
```

Maria: ah yeah — union narrowing + Optional is messy. pyright accepts the `isinstance(m.tags, list)` path; mypy needs Literal types sometimes. also the autogen using `list[str]` vs `List[str]` depending on py<3.9 compat can trigger different checks
Chris: iirc our autogen has a flag to prefer Sequence[...] over concrete list — that would narrow less but be more stable for typecheckers. also we need to ensure types are Optional[Sequence[str] | str] vs Optional[Union[str, Sequence[str]]]
Elaine: fwiw we also saw retries hitting a fast-fail path because the generated client typed `body: dict | None` and an earlier auth middleware expected Mapping[str, Any]. pyright accepted the narrower union and the runtime passed through but mypy tests caught a runtime mismatch in the sampleapp tests
Nate: hmm — so two things: (1) make autogen produce parity-friendly type form (Sequence vs list, explicit Union ordering), (2) update client/middleware type annotations to stronger protocols (Mapping/Sequence) to avoid accidental double-json dumps
Maria: proposed quick hack in the generator: coerce collection types to typing.Sequence and prefer explicit `Union[str, Sequence[str]]` (i've got a local branch). patch snippet:

```diff
- tags: Optional[Union[str, list[str]]]
+ from typing import Sequence
+ tags: Optional[Union[str, Sequence[str]]]
```

Chris: nice. also add a py.typed marker and run both mypy and pyright in CI matrix. we've only run mypy historically
Tyler: +1 on CI matrix. add an env matrix key: {python: 3.10, checker: mypy}, {python: 3.11, checker: pyright}
Elaine: small gotcha — pyright's strictness on `isinstance(..., list)` vs `Sequence` means some runtime isinstance checks will stop working if we move to Sequence. suggestion: generator should emit helper predicates for runtime checks, e.g., `is_list_like(x)` that uses isinstance(x, list) at runtime but keeps typing as Sequence
Nate: good point. runtime helpers will keep semantics and avoid churn in calling code. can we instead emit typed overloads for methods that accept both str and Sequence[str]? that would give callers better DX
Maria: overloads will be noisy in generated code. i'd rather keep a small helper + type guards (typing_extensions.TypeGuard) — then mypy & pyright will both understand narrowings
Chris: example typeguard helper:

```py
from typing import Any, Sequence
from typing_extensions import TypeGuard

def _is_list_like(x: Any) -> TypeGuard[Sequence[str]]:
    return isinstance(x, list)
```

Nate: perfect. then autogen can use `_is_list_like(m.tags)` in branch to satisfy both checkers
Tyler: action items? assign me to CI update PR. create an issue for generator changes
Maria: i'll open a generator PR with: convert collection types to Sequence, add TypeGuard helpers, add unit tests that run mypy+pyright. i'll include a small sampleapp integration test that streams responses (async) to cover async iterator typing
Elaine: also add a retry/auth integration test: ensure middleware accepts Mapping[str, Any] and that client body typing is Mapping | None rather than plain dict — reduces type drift
Chris: created issue #4321 in repo (autogen: prefer Sequence + TypeGuard helpers for collection unions). linking in thread: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4321
